issues.description: The problem statement defines Genre with a property named `name`, and the Client code constructs and accesses `Genre(name: ...)` and `genre.name`. However, the solution's Genre struct declares the property as `genreName`, causing a mismatch between the data model and how it is used. This will prevent code that expects `name` from compiling and confuses students about the correct property name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Genre property in Bookstore.swift from `genreName` to `name` (i.e. `let name: String`) so it matches the problem statement and the Client usage, or alternatively update Client and all call sites to use `genreName` and `Genre(genreName: ...)`. Prefer changing the struct to `let name: String` to align with the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies that Genre has a String property named 'name', and the Client code constructs and accesses genres using 'name' (e.g. Genre(name: ...) and genre.name). In the solution's Bookstore.swift the Genre struct instead declares the property as 'genreName'. This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual property (the genre's name) creates a mapping/confusion problem and will cause compilation errors or make it unclear which identifier to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the Genre name across all artifacts. Prefer changing the Genre struct property to 'name' (let name: String) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift and update any references accordingly, or alternatively update the problem statement and Client code to use 'genreName' everywhere. Aligning on 'name' is the least intrusive fix and matches the problem description.
